descricao_original: Bone tissue is classified based on two features: (1) its macroscopic appearance, i.e., how it appears to the naked eye, as either compact (cortical) or spongy (cancellous) and (2) its stage of maturation as either woven (immature) or lamellar (mature). A complete classification of bone tissue includes one term from each set, e.g., compact, woven bone or spongy, lamellar bone. 400x (all)

marcadores.explicacao_original: The matrix of lamellar bone is organized into lamellae that can be arranged as concentric layers forming osteons; flattened plates on the internal and external surfaces of a bone; or as parallel plates forming spicules of spongy bone. Woven compact and spongy bone are gradually remodeled into lamellar bone.
